scenes.heading: Cellular respiration
scenes.sub: How your cells turn glucose into ATP
scenes.say: Every cell needs a steady supply of ATP. Cellular respiration releases the energy in glucose and captures it as ATP. It even explains how yeast makes bread rise.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: A gift card swapped for a little cash and lots of vouchers
scenes.science: Glucose gives a little ATP and lots of NADH and FADH₂
scenes.breaks: a voucher has a fixed value, but the ATP from each NADH or FADH₂ isn't exact, so the total is a range (about 30–32).
scenes.say: Think of glucose as a gift card you can't spend directly. The early stages give a little cash straight away, but mostly vouchers: NADH and FADH two. The electron transport chain is where the vouchers get cashed in for most of the ATP.
scenes.caption: Think of glucose as a gift card you can't spend directly. The early stages give a little cash straight away, but mostly vouchers: NADH and FADH₂. The electron transport chain is where the vouchers get cashed in for most of the ATP.

scenes.heading: Aerobic respiration
scenes.say: Overall, glucose plus six oxygen gives six carbon dioxide plus six water, and about thirty to thirty-two ATP.
scenes.caption: Overall, glucose + 6 O₂ gives 6 CO₂ + 6 H₂O, and about 30–32 ATP.

scenes.heading: Three stages
scenes.say: Remember Cats Make Coffee: cytosol, matrix, cristae. Glycolysis in the cytosol makes two ATP. The Krebs cycle in the matrix releases carbon dioxide and makes two more. The electron transport chain on the cristae makes about twenty-six to twenty-eight.
scenes.caption: Remember Cats Make Coffee: cytosol, matrix, cristae. Glycolysis in the cytosol makes 2 ATP. The Krebs cycle in the matrix releases CO₂ and makes 2 more. The electron transport chain on the cristae makes about 26–28.

scenes.heading: The electron transport chain
points: NADH and FADH₂ unload electrons and H⁺
Energy pumps H⁺ across the inner membrane
H⁺ flows back through ATP synthase
Oxygen is the final electron acceptor
scenes.say: Here, NADH and FADH two unload electrons. Their energy pumps hydrogen ions across the inner membrane, like water behind a dam. The ions flow back through ATP synthase, making ATP. Oxygen is the final electron acceptor, forming water.
scenes.caption: Here, NADH and FADH₂ unload electrons. Their energy pumps H⁺ across the inner membrane, like water behind a dam. The H⁺ flows back through ATP synthase, making ATP. Oxygen is the final electron acceptor, forming water.

scenes.heading: Without oxygen: fermentation
scenes.say: Without oxygen, fermentation recycles NAD plus so glycolysis can keep making two ATP. Muscles make lactic acid. Yeast makes ethanol and carbon dioxide.
scenes.caption: Without oxygen, fermentation recycles NAD⁺ so glycolysis can keep making 2 ATP. Muscles make lactic acid. Yeast makes ethanol and CO₂.

scenes.heading: Worked example
scenes.question: Cyanide stops electrons being passed to oxygen. Predict the effect on a mammal's cells.
lines: ETC stops: almost no ATP made there
NADH and FADH₂ can't be unloaded
No NAD⁺ or FAD, so Krebs cycle stops
Only 2 ATP per glucose; lactic acid builds
scenes.say: Cyanide blocks the electron transport chain. Coenzymes can't be unloaded, so the Krebs cycle stops too. Cells get just two ATP per glucose, lactic acid builds up, and the heart and brain fail quickly.

points: Oxygen is the final electron acceptor
Animals: lactic acid; yeast: ethanol + CO₂
scenes.say: Quick recap. Three stages: cytosol, matrix, cristae. About thirty to thirty-two ATP per glucose. Oxygen is the final electron acceptor. Fermentation gives only two. Now try the practice questions!
